 Early voting in Delaware begins Thursday. Here’s what to know 
 by 
 Julia Merola 
 October 21, 2026 October 20, 2026

 A 10-day early voting period begins Thursday, Oct. 20, allowing voters to cast their ballots ahead of the Nov. 3 general election. | SPOTLIGHT DELAWARE PHOTO BY JACOB OWENS 
 Why Should Delaware Care? 
Early voting locations will be open 10 days before Election Day, giving Delawareans a chance to make their voice heard in the 2026 midterm election. The early voting period gives voters a chance to skip potential lines on Election Day and eases the process.
 While Delaware still is 13 days out from the 2026 midterm election on Nov. 3, voters can cast their ballot as early as Thursday. 
 Up for grabs in the consequential election are seats up and down the Delaware ballot, including for U.S. Senate, House of Representatives, Delaware attorney general and treasurer, and dozens of statehouse positions.
 All registered Delaware voters can vote early in their county of residence. To do so, they must present at the polling station one of the following: a state-issued photo ID, a utility bill, or a government document with the voter’s name and address
 To be eligible, voters must be a U.S. citizen, a Delaware resident and 18 years old or older by Election Day.
 For information about candidates, visit Spotlight Delaware’s 2026 Election Center .
 When can I vote early?  
 Early voting locations will be open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. from Oct. 22 through Oct. 27 – except on Sunday, Oct. 25, when they will close. 
 From Oct. 28 through Nov. 1, they will be open between 11 a.m. to 7 p.m.
 Where can I vote early? 
 Not all polling locations in the state will be open for early voting. Instead, there will be six designated locations in New Castle County, four in Kent County, and nine in Sussex County. 
 Delawareans can vote at any early voting location within their county.
 The polling locations are as follows: 
 New Castle County 
 Appoquinimink State Service Center, 122 Silver Lake Road, Middletown, DE 19709
 Claymont Community Center, 3301 Green St., Claymont, DE 19703
 The Delaware Contemporary, 200 S. Madison St., Wilmington, DE 19801
 Department of Elections Warehouse – New Castle, 220 Lisa Drive, New Castle, DE 19720
 Hudson State Service Center, 501 Ogletown Road, Newark, DE 19711
 Police Athletic League (PAL), 3707 N. Market St., Wilmington, DE 19802
 Kent County 
 BPOE #1903 Elks Lodge, 200 S Saulsbury Road, Dover, DE 19904
 Frederica Senior Center, 216 Market St., Frederica, DE 19946
 Harrington Parks & Recreation, 114 E. Liberty St., Harrington, DE 19952
 Wyoming United Methodist Church, 216 Wyoming Mill Rd., Dover, DE 19904
 Sussex County 
 Department of Elections Warehouse – Georgetown, 542 S. Bedford St., Georgetown DE 19947
 Department of Elections Warehouse – Seaford, 200 Allen St., Seaford, DE 19973
 Ellendale Fire Hall, 302 Main St., Ellendale, DE 19941
 Indian River Fire Company, 25375 Banks Rd., Millsboro, DE 19966
 Laurel Fire Hall, 205 W. 10th St., Laurel, DE 19956
 Margaret H. Rollins Community Center, 101 Adams Ave., Lewes, DE 19958 
 Millville Community Center, 32517 Dukes Drive, Millville, DE 19967
 Nassau Valley Vineyard, 32130 Winery Rd., Lewes, DE 19958
 Roxana Fire Hall, 35943 Zion Church Rd., Frankford, DE 19945
 Can I request an absentee ballot? 
 If you can’t vote at a polling location – whether early or on Election Day – you can vote by absentee ballot if you have a reason permitted by the state. Those include being sick or disabled, being a caregiver who can’t leave their home, or being stationed abroad in the armed services. More information on whether you qualify can be found here .  
 To request an absentee ballot, visit Delaware iVote portal, then download and return the absentee ballot request form, found here .
 Absentee ballots must be received by the Department of Elections at 8 p.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 3, in order to count.
 What if I have a question or an issue at the poll? 
 If you need help or need to speak with an elections official about your registration or voting options, contact the Delaware Department of Elections in your relevant county. Click here to find phone numbers and emails for those offices.
 If you notice an issue at the polls and want to bring it to Spotlight Delaware’s attention, email tips@spotlightdelaware.org . Include as much detail as you can, including where, when, and what you observed. Please include contact info, even if you wish to remain anonymous in our reporting, so that we can follow up and learn more about the situation.
